G-DPA_1.title: Data Processing Agreements
G-DPA_1.description: Maintain a register of every processor that handles personal data on your behalf, with a signed DPA. Art. 28(3) requires the contract to set out the subject-matter and duration of the processing, its nature and purpose, the type of personal data and the categories of data subjects, before it reaches the eight clauses in points (a) to (h).

G-DPA_2.title: Sub-processor Authorisation
G-DPA_2.description: Track each processor's sub-processors. Art. 28(2) requires the controller's prior specific or general written authorisation before a processor engages another one. Art. 28(4) is a second duty: the same Art. 28(3) obligations must be imposed on the sub-processor by contract, and the initial processor stays fully liable for its performance.

G-ROP_1.title: Records of Processing Activities
G-ROP_1.description: Record each processing activity with the seven Art. 30(1) entries: controller and DPO contacts, purposes, categories of data subjects and of personal data, recipient categories, third-country transfers with safeguards and, where possible, erasure periods and a description of the measures. Art. 30(5) exempts organisations employing fewer than 250 persons, but only where the processing is occasional, is unlikely to result in a risk to rights and freedoms, and involves no special categories or criminal conviction data. Regular personnel and payroll processing is not occasional, so in practice the record is still owed.

G-TOM_1.title: Technical and Organisational Measures
G-TOM_1.description: Document the measures protecting personal data: pseudonymisation and encryption, lasting confidentiality, integrity, availability and resilience, timely restoration after an incident, and a process for regularly testing and evaluating their effectiveness (Art. 32(1)).

G-BRC_1.title: Personal Data Breach Response Process
G-BRC_1.description: Establish a written procedure for assessing personal data breaches and notifying the supervisory authority without undue delay and, where feasible, within 72 hours (Art. 33(1)). Notification is not owed where the breach is unlikely to result in a risk to the rights and freedoms of natural persons, so the procedure has to record that assessment either way. A filing made after 72 hours must state the reasons for the delay.

G-BRC_2.title: Personal Data Breach Documentation
G-BRC_2.description: Internally document every personal data breach (notifiable or not) for supervisory-authority verification (Art. 33(5)).

G-DSR_1.title: Data Subject Rights Workflow
G-DSR_1.description: Process for handling access, erasure, rectification, portability, restriction and objection requests within one month (Art. 12-22). For a German controller §34 BDSG restricts the Art. 15 right of access, and §35 substitutes restriction of processing for Art. 17 erasure where non-automated storage makes deletion disproportionate. §34(2) requires the reasons for refusing access to be documented.

G-BRC_3.title: Communication to affected data subjects
G-BRC_3.description: Define the process for telling affected individuals about a breach that is likely to result in a high risk to them (Art. 34(1)). Notifying the supervisory authority under Art. 33 does not discharge it. The communication uses clear and plain language and carries the information in Art. 33(3)(b) to (d). It is not required where the data was rendered unintelligible (for example by encryption), where the high risk has since been mitigated, or where the effort would be disproportionate, in which case a public communication is required instead (Art. 34(3)).

G-DPO_1.title: Designate a data protection officer
G-DPO_1.description: Assess and document whether a data protection officer must be designated. In Germany the duty starts at 20 persons constantly engaged in the automated processing of personal data (§38(1) BDSG), and applies regardless of headcount where processing requires a data protection impact assessment or is carried out commercially for the purpose of transfer or of market and opinion research. Position and tasks follow Art. 38 and 39 GDPR; the contact details must be published and communicated to the supervisory authority (Art. 37(7)).
